The rapid growth of digital content has motivated extensive research on personalized recommendation systems to alleviate information overload [S2:1be97c1d9ace0363f8f612ca1be3d4fb33e177bb][S2:81adb8a188204880b8cc3ebfda674c2d240563b3]. Graph neural networks have emerged as a versatile tool for modeling complex user‑item interactions in recommendation tasks [S2:1be97c1d9ace0363f8f612ca1be3d4fb33e177bb][S2:e7c7442bac762d0e8d22e385a57ec76e1e5c0c4c]. Recent efforts such as DAPEW explore graph contrastive learning to enhance the robustness of collaborative filtering models [S2:81adb8a188204880b8cc3ebfda674c2d240563b3].

Neural Graph Collaborative Filtering introduced a message‑passing architecture that propagates collaborative signals beyond directly observed interactions [S2:c5f5f179d80a3bf9b4f29750283a87eaca42e91b]. Beyond Graph Structure presented a simplified spectral‑aware contrastive approach that builds on NGCF’s message‑passing foundation to improve scalability [S2:46da64f666499c0e6559c3b3d374fc7d07675332]. Profiling the Design Space for Graph Neural Networks based Collaborative Filtering systematically evaluated three layer‑combination strategies—Concat, Sum, and Mean—extending the architectural choices explored in NGCF [S2:a2a42052eb8c0dd5ee339877b37f135fdfea00bd]. A reproducibility study of SIGIR 2022 recommender papers standardized the evaluation protocol for message‑passing models, reinforcing the experimental settings originally used by NGCF [S2:4920370543dcf58da4f3ab7de03508762098b276].

Revisiting Graph based Collaborative Filtering proposed a linear residual GCN that simplifies graph convolutions while retaining performance, extending earlier GCN‑based recommender designs [S2:c9e432023a240b22f385cf1cc76ab75fbe084ee7].
